Resolves #21441

The Bash push guard now blocks a `git push` whose refspec holds a colon, in any shell form: `git -C <dir> push`, `cd <dir> && git push`, or a push inside a pipe or a substitution. Its message names the form that works, `git push -u origin <branch>`. Until now the settings glob `Bash(git push* *:*)` caught only the literal `git push …` prefix. The other forms reached the auto-mode classifier and came back as "Undermining Oversight", with nothing a seat could act on.

How it works: `gitInvocations()` keeps each git invocation's arguments up to the end of its simple command. `pushRefspecs()` reads the words the way `git push` does. The first positional is the repository, even when `--repo` names one, and the rest are refspecs. A value option reads the next word: `-o` at the end of a short group (`-uo ci:skip`), and `--repo`, `--recurse-submodules`, `--receive-pack`, `--exec` and `--push-option`, by name or unambiguous abbreviation. `--` ends the options, and redirections don't count. So a URL remote, `--push-option=ci:skip` or `-uo ci:skip` never trips the guard. The commit-and-push check is unchanged.

Evidence: L2 (unit spec over the guard's decisions, plus the same probe on `dev` and at the head) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-4). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/hooks/gitCommitPushGuardHook.spec.mjs` › "a push that names a colon refspec is blocked in every shell form, the ones the settings glob misses included" |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec › "a push by branch name passes, and a colon outside a refspec never counts", and › "a push reads its words the way git does: option values are skipped and the first positional is the repository" |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the spec's existing commit-and-push tests pass unchanged |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/hooks` in the `unit` job; locally, `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/hooks/` passes 45/45 at the head |

## Deltas from ticket

- `redirectionGuardHook.mjs` exports its `SEPARATORS` set. The new parse ends an invocation where the other guards end a command, instead of keeping a copy of the set.
- `--repo` turns no positional into a refspec: git takes the first positional as the repository either way (`git push -h`). So `--repo=<remote> <url> a:b` is caught by its `a:b`.

## Test Evidence

Base against head, with the same probe: `decideGitCommitPushGuard` on `git -C ../w push -u origin ada/1-x:ada/1-x` and on `cd ../w && git push origin a:a`. On `dev` both return `null` and reach the classifier; at this head both return `block`.

I could not exercise a live harness. This seat's generated `.claude/settings.json` (17 Nov) predates #21292 and registers no `gitCommitPushGuardHook`. That is out of scope here and noted in a defect-note.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Once a seat's `.claude/settings.json` is regenerated from the template, `git -C <clone> push --dry-run origin a:a` answers with the guard's message.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** An inert exact-head replay classified a positional `https://example.invalid/team/repo.git` as a refspec when `--repo` was also supplied. The same URL was misclassified after the separately passed `--recurse-submodules` operand `check`. A grouped short set-upstream/push-option flag after the repository also treats its `ci:skip` operand as a refspec. The ordinary URL, plain branch, literal-refspec and commit-plus-push controls behaved as before. No push was performed.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** The code follows the common shell tokenizer. It does not yet follow Git’s repository and option-operand parsing for these named forms.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

The parser needs to distinguish the repository from refspecs after option parsing, because colons are valid in repository and option values.

### 🎯 Close-Target Audit

**Findings:** #21441 is an enhancement leaf. Legitimate URL and push-option forms still fail AC-2.

### 📑 Contract Completeness Audit

**Findings:** [Git’s push manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push#Documentation/git-push.txt---repoltrepositorygt) gives positional repository precedence. [Git’s implementation](https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/builtin/push.c#L657-L718) consumes the submodule and push-option arguments before taking the first positional as the repository. [This guard](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/fa31c79c630ebcdc32c87f8c1d9dee6c34765677/.claude/hooks/gitCommitPushGuardHook.mjs#L80-L99) skips an incomplete option set and treats all remaining words as refspecs when `--repo` appears.
